chunks: Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to me, from his grandfather Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) said:
When a man prepares his shroud, he is rewarded every time he looks at it.

key_terms.كفن: Kafan (shroud) - the burial cloth used to wrap the deceased in Islamic funeral rites
key_terms.مأجور: Rewarded - one who receives divine reward (ajr) for their action

ai.seo_question: Is there reward in Islam for preparing your own burial shroud?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) taught that a person who prepares their burial shroud in advance receives ongoing divine reward each time they look at it. This narration, transmitted through the family chain of the Imams, reflects the Islamic practice of remembering death as a means of spiritual preparation and detachment from worldly attachments. In early Muslim society, preparing one's shroud was seen as an act of humility and readiness for the inevitable return to Allah.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ja`far b. `Ali b. al-Hasan b. `Ali b. `Abdullah b. al-Mughira al-Kufi (ra) narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan b. `Ali narrated to me from his grandfather `Abdullah b. al-Mughira from Isma`il b. Muslim from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as). He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said:
When a man prepares his shroud, he is rewarded for every time he looks at it.
